title: Opinion of bebop and modern music
summary: Lala says he cannot play or understand bebop, and the interviewer complains modern music has nothing new.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Matt Barton, there's a fella by the name of Matt Barton, you can't tell from this.
He's like that, what you call this, this bebop, I can't do it, you know? I don't understand. I don't like...

I can't play it. I said, I'm asking him, I said, what's that, what's that, what's that playin'? I don't know. I can't understand. I don't think the people who were playing it understand it themselves, you know? I can't do it. Tell me that kid of mine, that's all he wants to play. Who, Mike?

Yeah. He don't play on that. Well, you know, Johnny, look, I don't have it in for any kind of music. As a matter of fact, I love some classical music. I don't love all classical music. I mean, everybody's got a right to pick their music. Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah. The thing is that I have against the music which they call modern music, the music which is played mostly now, is that it does not have any interest. No. They don't have anything new. They think they have something new. No, they don't. But they don't have anything new, and it's very stilted and very uninteresting.
